project.name: libxml2
project.fuzz_target: xmllint HTML file parser (`--html --noout` reproduction path)

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 preserved the vulnerable libxml2 checkout used for reproduction. Its line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer frames at `HTMLparser.c:448`, `HTMLparser.c:457`, `HTMLparser.c:106`, and `error.c:529`.

classification.classification_note: The saved AddressSanitizer traces report a heap-use-after-free READ in `__xmlRaiseError` at `error.c:529`. Source analysis shows that `htmlFindEncoding()` allocates an attacker-derived encoding token, `htmlCurrentChar()` frees that buffer before checking whether `xmlFindCharEncodingHandler()` returned `NULL`, and the unsupported-encoding error path then passes the dangling pointer through `htmlParseErr()` into the `%s` formatting logic in `__xmlRaiseError()`.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in htmlCurrentChar (HTMLparser.c): an encoding name buffer is freed while still referenced by the HTML error reporting path (htmlParseErr / __xmlRaiseError), causing subsequent formatted error output to read freed heap memory. This can lead to crashes (denial of service) and may be exploitable for arbitrary code execution depending on context.
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a 35-byte HTML file whose exact bytes are eight spaces, byte `0xff`, and the ASCII tail `http-equIvcontentcharset=:`. `xmllint --html --noout` skips the leading blanks, treats the leading non-markup byte `0xff` as character data, and calls `htmlCurrentChar()` with `XML_INPUT_HAS_ENCODING` still clear. Because the same input buffer also contains case-insensitive matches for `HTTP-EQUIV`, `CONTENT`, and `CHARSET=`, `htmlFindEncoding()` duplicates the single-byte encoding token `:` into heap buffer `guess`. Vulnerable `htmlCurrentChar()` immediately frees `guess`, then discovers that `xmlFindCharEncodingHandler(":")` returned `NULL` and reports `Unsupported encoding %s` with the freed pointer. `htmlParseErr()` forwards that stale pointer to `__xmlRaiseError()`, and the saved AddressSanitizer report shows the resulting formatter read at `error.c:529`.

source.description: First project-code materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker data. After scanning the input buffer for case-insensitive `HTTP-EQUIV`, `CONTENT`, and `CHARSET=` tokens, this statement duplicates the attacker-controlled encoding name `:` into a heap buffer that later becomes dangling.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` bytes are `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff 68 74 74 70 2d 65 71 75 49 76 63 6f 6e 74 65 6e 74 63 68 61 72 73 65 74 3d 3a`, decoded as eight spaces, `0xff`, and `http-equIvcontentcharset=:`. `htmlFindEncoding()` matches those ASCII tokens case-insensitively and duplicates the single-character encoding token `:`.

sink.description: Crash sink. The generic error formatter expands `"Unsupported encoding %s"` using `str1`, which still points to the already-freed `guess` buffer, and AddressSanitizer records the resulting heap-use-after-free READ here.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. Vulnerable code frees the attacker-derived encoding buffer before the `handler == NULL` decision, even though the subsequent error-reporting branch still uses `guess` as the `%s` argument.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later dangling pointer originates when `htmlFindEncoding()` duplicates the attacker-controlled encoding token `:` into heap storage.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific HTML admission point. After the leading blanks, the witness presents byte `0xff`, which is neither `<`, `&`, nor `0`, so content parsing admits the remaining bytes as character data and enters the path that immediately calls `CUR_CHAR(l)`.

coarse_trace.summary: The saved HTML file is admitted as character data because its first non-blank byte is `0xff`, and char-data parsing calls `CUR_CHAR(l)` with input encoding still unspecified.

The same input buffer contains case-insensitive `HTTP-EQUIV`, `CONTENT`, and `CHARSET=` tokens, so `htmlFindEncoding()` allocates heap string `":"`, `htmlCurrentChar()` stores it in `guess`, and unsupported-encoding lookup returns `NULL`.
Vulnerable code frees `guess` too early, then the `handler == NULL` branch still calls `htmlParseErr("Unsupported encoding %s", guess, NULL)` with the stale pointer.
The HTML error helper forwards the dangling pointer into the generic formatter, and `XML_GET_VAR_STR` reads freed heap memory while expanding `%s`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer report.

fine_trace.note: After the leading blanks in the staged file, the current byte is attacker-controlled `0xff`, which is neither `<`, `&`, nor `0`, so HTML parsing admits the remaining bytes as character data and enters `htmlParseCharData()`.

Character-data parsing immediately requests the current character. Because the current byte is non-ASCII `0xff` and `XML_INPUT_HAS_ENCODING` is still clear, this dispatch reaches `htmlCurrentChar()`'s encoding-detection path.

Source. Scanning the same attacker-controlled buffer finds case-insensitive `HTTP-EQUIV`, `CONTENT`, and `CHARSET=` tokens and duplicates the one-byte encoding token `:` into freshly allocated heap storage.

depends_on.via: CUR_CHAR(l) reached htmlCurrentChar() with a non-ASCII current byte

fine_trace.note: The heap buffer returned by `htmlFindEncoding()` is aliased into local variable `guess`, which is the pointer later freed and then reused by the error path.
The attacker-derived encoding name `:` is looked up as a charset handler. That lookup yields `NULL`, making the unsupported-encoding error branch the next control decision.
Root cause. The heap buffer holding `:` is freed immediately after handler lookup, but `guess` still retains the freed address and the `handler == NULL` branch has not executed yet.
Because `xmlFindCharEncodingHandler(":")` returned `NULL`, control falls through to the `else` branch that reports an unsupported encoding instead of switching encodings.
The unsupported-encoding branch passes the already-freed `guess` pointer as `str1` for the `%s` placeholder in the HTML error message.

fine_trace.code:
__xmlRaiseError(NULL, NULL, NULL, ctxt, NULL, XML_FROM_HTML, error,
                XML_ERR_ERROR, NULL, 0,
                (const char *) str1, (const char *) str2,
                NULL, 0, 0,
                msg, str1, str2);
fine_trace.note: The HTML error wrapper forwards the same stale pointer into `__xmlRaiseError()` as the first variable formatting argument for `msg`.
Sink. Formatting `"Unsupported encoding %s"` consumes `str1` as the `%s` argument and reads freed heap memory from the buffer that formerly held `:`. The saved AddressSanitizer reports the read here.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the reconstructed root cause because it moves `xmlFree(guess);` after both the successful-switch and error-reporting branches in `htmlCurrentChar()`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, exact staged vulnerable source, and the saved poc

poc.trigger: Run the saved file through the staged HTML parser path with `./xmllint --html --noout /gt/poc`; the witness makes `htmlFindEncoding()` allocate `guess = ":"`, frees it in `htmlCurrentChar()`, and immediately reuses that pointer in the unsupported-encoding error message.

format.name: HTML text document with faux HTTP-EQUIV charset declaration
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged file: eight leading space bytes, then byte `0xff`, then the ASCII tail `http-equIvcontentcharset=:`. On this witness, HTML parsing skips the blanks, treats `0xff` as character data with no encoding fixed yet, and `htmlFindEncoding()` case-insensitively matches `HTTP-EQUIV`, `CONTENT`, and `CHARSET=` inside the same buffer so that it duplicates the one-byte unsupported encoding token `:`.
